title: SE301 Lesson 1: Size the model, then run the first endpoint
status: Script and facts await Clark's review. Do not narrate until he says yes. No media has been rendered.

scenes.text: Your model fits on paper. Can your laptop still answer after you cancel its first stream? Start with a memory budget. Finish with two requests you can replay.

data.headline:
Size the model.
Then run the first endpoint.
data.sub: Run your own AI studio  •  clarkhuang.github.io

scenes.text: Quick question. Before you download a local model, what do you check? [pause] The product name? The memory on the sticker? Or the weight floor, with room left over? [pause] <emphasis>The floor, with room left over.</emphasis> The sticker is the whole machine.

data.question:
Before the download,
what do you check?
data.why:
The sticker is
the whole machine.
The model gets
what’s left.

scenes.text: Start with the weight floor. Parameter count, times bits per weight, divided by eight. [pause] That is gigabytes of weights, and only weights. Eighty billion parameters, at four bits, starts at forty gigabytes. Three hundred twenty billion starts at one hundred sixty. Four hundred eighty billion starts at two hundred forty.

The floor is not the whole bill. Add metadata, the runtime, the operating system, your other programs, and a context cache for each open session. [pause] A two hundred forty gigabyte floor is a poor everyday choice on a two hundred fifty six gigabyte host.

data.label: HEADROOM  ·  THE FLOOR IS NOT THE BILL
data.left: Almost nothing left for the OS, the runtime, or a context cache.

scenes.text: Load a small model first. On an Apple silicon Mac you already own, try a three to eight billion parameter model, four bit, only if memory permits. [pause] The playbook's first fixture, on its forty eight gigabyte laptop, is Qwen two point five Coder, seven B, Instruct, four bit. If gpt oss twenty b is already working, compare it. Don't download it in order to start.

data.label: THE PLAYBOOK’S LADDER  ·  SMALL MODEL FIRST
rows: gpt-oss-20b, same tasks, not a new download

scenes.text: These Studio candidates need testing on the actual hardware. Keep your small laptop baseline for comparison.

data.label: 512 GB STUDIO  ·  CANDIDATES, NOT MEASUREMENTS
data.foot: Hardware is ordered. Throughput, power, and usable context come later.

scenes.text: When it loads, run one prompt at four K, at sixteen K, and at thirty two K. Write down peak memory, swap, time to first token, and output tokens per second. <slow>Stop when the wait misses your target.</slow>

data.label: SAME PROMPT  ·  THREE CONTEXT LENGTHS
data.foot: Stop when interactive latency misses your target.

scenes.text: Then build the endpoint. Write down the machine and the free disk. Install one pinned llmster runtime, and one model that fits. Bind it to loopback. One two seven point zero point zero point one. Not the open network. [pause] Send a completion, a stream, a cancel, and a tool call. Save them with the model manifest. <emphasis>A chat reply does not prove the tools.</emphasis>

data.label: THE FIRST ENDPOINT  ·  LOOPBACK ONLY
items: Write down the machine and free disk
One pinned llmster, one model that fits
data.foot: A chat reply does not prove the tools.

scenes.text: Try this on your own endpoint. Ask for the numbers one through twenty, one per line, with streaming turned on. Watch for the first piece before the final one. Cancel halfway. Then send a fresh request: reply with the word ready. Save what actually happened on both requests. A stopped display alone cannot tell you whether the server stopped computing. Check the runtime log before you mark that part as passed.

data.label: REPLAY CARD  ·  TRY IT ON YOUR ENDPOINT
steps: Stream
Count from 1 to 20, one number per line.
Observe
Did output arrive before the final event?
Cancel
Stop the client during the stream.
Retry
New request: reply with the word ready.
Check
Save the reply and the server log.

scenes.text: One prompt on this page drives a computer-use agent, or a terminal agent, on a Mac or a P.C. [pause] It reads the operating system, the C.P.U., the G.P.U., the memory, and free disk. It picks a tier. It installs llmster, or M.L.X. on Apple silicon, or Ollama on a P.C. It sends one live request. Then it waits.

data.label: THE COPY-PASTE PROMPT  ·  ON-SCREEN SUMMARY
steps: Read the machine
OS, CPU, GPU, memory, free disk
Pick a tier
From this ladder. Show the arithmetic.
Install one runtime
llmster, MLX on Apple silicon, or Ollama
Send one request
To the local endpoint. Read the reply.
Stop for you
Name the action. Wait for a yes.

scenes.text: <slow>It waits before any admin install, any firewall change, and any sign-in.</slow> You name the action, and you say yes. Silence is not a yes. [pause] Don't paste a key, a token, or a password. Don't send a local file off the machine. The smoke test is one short sentence, to loopback. The reply stays on your computer.

data.label: THE PROMPT STOPS
nevers: No local files off the machine
data.foot: Silence is not a yes. The reply stays on your computer.

scenes.text: Rule one, for your agents. Before a download, write the weight floor, the memory you can spare, and the check that says the endpoint answered. Put that note where the agent can read it. Admin rights, a firewall change, or a sign-in: stop and ask.

and the check that says the endpoint answered.
Admin, firewall, or sign-in? Stop and ask.

data.foot: THE FULL RULE IS ON THE LESSON PAGE

scenes.text: Your turn. Open the prompt. Let the agent show you the tier it chose. [pause] Say yes only to the install you understand. Keep the reply. That reply is your baseline.
